keywords: South Cotabato Improved Tiniguib corn variety
excerpt: South Cotabato Improved Tiniguib corn is a white open pollinated corn variety, also sold or known as Tupi 1 White Improved Tiniguib or Tupi 1 WIT. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2023 as NSIC 2023 Cn 337. Department of Agriculture Regional Field Office XII bred it. It takes 104 to 108 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain, with 5.16 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Tupi 1 White Improved Tiniguib or Tupi 1 WIT, this is the same corn. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [corn variety finder](/crop-varieties/corn), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

South Cotabato Improved Tiniguib corn takes 104 to 108 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. That is about the average of the 28 white open pollinated corn varieties with a day count, 103 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 5.16 t/ha trails the average of its group, 5.36. One tonne of shelled corn fills about 20 sacks of 50 kilograms. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 104 (dry season) to 108 (wet season) in NSIC trials.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer).

The pests and diseases that hit corn fields most often: [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [banded leaf and sheath blight](/diseases/banded-leaf-and-sheath-blight), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn ear rot](/diseases/corn-ear-rot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its ears grew about 14.43 cm long in the trials. The shelling recovery was 79 percent, the share of the ear weight that comes off as grain. A higher share means more grain from every sack of ears.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 5.15 t/ha average, above the 4.98 t/ha Mindanao check.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: launched by DA BAR in December 2023 under the CGUARD program and handed out to Mindanao farmers (DA RFO12, Inquirer). Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant South Cotabato Improved Tiniguib corn

The registry recommends it for Mindanao. Start with the color your buyer pays for: yellow corn goes to feed mills, while white and glutinous corn go to the table. Next, pick between a hybrid, which yields more but needs new seed every season, and an open pollinated variety, whose seed you can save. Then match the island group in its recommendation, because trials in Luzon and Mindanao give different winners. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for corn](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

items.q: Is Tupi 1 White Improved Tiniguib the same as South Cotabato Improved Tiniguib?
items.a: Yes. Tupi 1 White Improved Tiniguib is another name for South Cotabato Improved Tiniguib, registered as NSIC 2023 Cn 337. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 104 to 108 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 5.16 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.
The registry recommends it for Mindanao. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of South Cotabato Improved Tiniguib?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
